# Research

::: {.lead}
I work on market design, matching theory and empirical methods. Working on real allocation procedures with municipalities and states generates data that allow their effects to be studied causally. I use administrative data and field experiments from Germany, Hungary and England.
:::
:::

## Research areas

::: {.cards .three}
::: {.card-c .has-img}
![](/assets/img/cards/harvard.jpg){.card-img}

::: {.card-body}
### School choice

**Parents in the lab.** All mechanisms are frequently manipulated, by parents about as often as by students. [arXiv 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24615)

**Efficiency and strategy-proofness.** In Budapest, the Rank-Minimizing mechanism cuts the share of poor placements from 15 to under 3 per cent. [GEB 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geb.2023.07.008)

**Childcare.** Decentralised deferred acceptance for childcare [JMID 2021](http://www.mechanism-design.org/arch/v006-1/p_03.pdf).
:::
:::


::: {.card-c .has-img}
![](/assets/img/cards/kita.png){.card-img}

::: {.card-body}
### Inequality

**Shadow education.** When children are assigned to the top track, families from the lowest socio-economic tercile increase private tutoring disproportionately. [DP 2025](https://ftp.zew.de/pub/zew-docs/dp/dp25023.pdf)

**Early tracking.** Academic-track schools help children of all backgrounds, but disadvantaged children are less likely to get there. [DP 2024](https://ftp.zew.de/pub/zew-docs/dp/dp24076.pdf)

**School choice across districts.** When districts merge their allocation, everyone gains on average; the gain is equivalent to a school five kilometres closer. [GEB 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geb.2024.07.003)
:::
:::

::: {.card-c .has-img}
![](/assets/img/cards/esaf.jpg){.card-img}

::: {.card-body}
### Development economics

**Microfinance.** In Thailand, more diverse borrower groups improve repayment by ten percentage points. [DP 2024](https://ftp.zew.de/pub/zew-docs/dp/dp24070.pdf)

**Statistics and data.** Work from my OECD years (2014–2017) on the value of official statistics and new data sources.
:::
